title: evening-peak-burst-replay-validation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Build and validate a long-duration steady-burst replay harness that reproduces realistic evening-peak traffic patterns against Dedicated capacity pools. This ticket covers harness design, metric instrumentation, pass/fail criteria, and an automated regression detector that flags p95 latency and tokens/sec anomalies during steady-state and short high-intensity bursts.

Context: Several customer workloads run heavy inference during evening windows (region-specific). We need a repeatable test that: (1) replays representative request mixes across model variants, (2) holds steady throughput for 30–90 minutes to exercise autoscaler decisions and padding/kv-cache behavior, and (3) injects short 90–120s burst windows at 10–20x base QPS to validate graceful scaling and fallbacks. Current related work: ENG-12977 (oscillation detection) and ENG-11024 (hybrid load generator).

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Harness can run against a dedicated pool with per-GPU token/sec target and scale to N replicas via the autoscaler without violating p95 latency SLO (> 95th percentile must stay below configured SLO).
- Record tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, request error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and queue depth at 10s granularity.
- Regression detector must compare a run against a rolling baseline (last 10 successful runs) using EWMA on p95 and tokens/sec and signal if deviation > 15% for tokens/sec or > 20% of SLO for p95 for more than 3 consecutive minutes.
- Burst validation: simulate 3 distinct burst profiles (short spike 90s, medium spike 3m, stagged ramp 6m) and ensure autoscaler responds without >10% sustained error rate or catastrophic model fallbacks.
- Test produces an artifact with: raw metrics (CSV), aggregated summary, Datadog/Prometheus dashboard link, and a GitHub PR template to run the harness in CI/nightly.

Design notes and instrumentation:
- Replay source: sampled production traces anonymized and normalized to fixed prompt lengths for deterministic tokens/sec calculation. For synthetic variance, include a distribution of prompt lengths: 64 tokens (40%), 256 tokens (40%), 1024 tokens (20%).
- Load controller: a stateful runner (k8s job) that emits requests through Redwood API test keys, supports multi-model routing and pinned model variants. It will target per-GPU tokens/sec by tracking tokens generated per response and throttling clients to meet target.
- Metrics sink: push histograms and counters to Prometheus; export summarized CSV to S3 after run. Label metrics by pool_id, model_variant, run_id, and phase (steady|burst).
- Regression algorithm: compute EWMA (alpha=0.2) for p95 and tokens/sec per model_variant over the baseline window. Flag run as degraded when both: (a) current EWMA deviation exceeds threshold, or (b) non-parametric Mann-Whitney U test p-value < 0.01 between baseline and current p95 samples. This hybrid approach reduces sensitivity to transient noise.
- Alerting: when regression detector fires, create an incident draft with relevant run artifacts and triage checklist (links to PRs, console traces, model variant, pool topology).

Run plan and schedule:
- Phase 1 (week 1): implement basic runner, metric plumbing, and steady-state profile (30m at target tokens/sec). Smoke runs against staging dedicated pool.
- Phase 2 (week 2): add burst profiles, regression detector, dashboarding, and automated artifact export.
- Phase 3 (week 3): harden harness, add CI job to run nightly against a minimal dedicated pool, and document runbook.

Acceptance tests (manual/automated):
- Nightly job produces no regression alerts for at least 5 consecutive runs under controlled staging config.
- Injected fault (artificially increase latency by 30%) must cause detector to fire and CI to mark the run as failed.

Operational considerations and cost:
- Expected resource usage for a single 3-hour run against medium pool: ~6 GPU-hours. Cost estimate attached. Avoid running against prod capacity without prior coordination.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Evening+Peak+Replay+Harness
- Dashboard (Datadog): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/xxxx/evening-peak-replay
- Example PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/placeholder
